previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, hepatitis C, and alcohol dependence was admitted for acute shortness of breath and volume overload after again missing his heart failure medications. He had gained nearly 30 pounds since his last discharge and showed signs of fluid retention. A chest X-ray revealed mild pulmonary vascular congestion and cardiomegaly, and his proBNP was markedly elevated. He received IV furosemide and was monitored for alcohol withdrawal, with a peak CIWA score of 15. He declined staying for electrolyte monitoring but agreed to follow-up. He was discharged home on his baseline heart failure regimen with strong counseling to adhere to medications and avoid alcohol.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with chronic sCHF (LVEF ___ 
in ___ and AF who presented, after a recent hospitalization 
for decompensated sCHF from which he left AMA, with dyspnea and 
a weight gain in setting of medication non-compliance. He was 
diuresed with a lasix gtt with some improvement in symptoms. On 
hospital day two patient left AMA despite instructions regarding 
the dangers of leaving. 

PUMP: LVEF ___
CORONARIES: One vessel CAD (Left Cx)
RHYTHM: afib

ACTIVE ISSUES: 
==================
# Acute on Chronic Systolic CHF: Hemodynamically stable without 
signs of end-organ hypoperfusion. Evidenced by dyspnea with 
consistent exam findings, elevated proBNP, and CXR evidence. 
Several recent admissions for the same. Etiology of acute flare 
is most likely medication non-compliance, as he is not taking 
any medications at all. No acute ischemic changes on EKG and 
negative troponins. He digressed well with a lasix gtt but left 
AMA with signs of being acutely volume overloaded.
# COPD: Possible exacerbation as evidenced by cough with 
intermittent sputum production over the past few days in 
association with his worsening dyspnea. Clinical picture is 
clouded by his acute on chronic CHF as above - given that 
prednisone would not be benign amidst his CHF flare and that his 
QTc is already borderline at 485, we held off on further 
prednisone (s/p 60mg po in ED).
# Afib with RVR: Hemodynamically stable. Etiology most likely 
due to acute on chronic CHF as above in addition to ongoing 
heavy EtOH use. Continued rivaroxaban.
# Transaminitis, possible cirrhosis: Chronic though elevated 
over baseline. Etiology likely multifactorial from current CHF 
exacerbation in addition to heavy EtOH use. Last admission note 
reports HCV as well however review of Micro data has several 
negative HCV RNA assays. Pt with thrombocytopenia, echogenic 
liver on u/s, and interval increase in splenomegaly to roughly 
15cm - together findings were concerning for possible 
cirrhosis/portal hypertension. No ascites to sample. 
# ___: Mild creatinine elevation to 1.3 from baseline 1.1, which 
in association with his mild hyponatremia is likely due to acute 
on chronic CHF with elevated venous pressures. Creatinine 
improved with diuresis.
# EtOH: Heavy ingestion with high risk of withdrawal. Was 
monitored on CIWA with diazepam 10mg po prn CIWA >10. Continued 
thiamine/folate PO.
# Psychosocial: Seen by social Work for substance use, 
homelessness, and medication non-compliance. These are central 
to all of the medical issues above.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital because you had some shortness 
of breath from your heart failure. You received IV medicines to 
get the water out of your lungs. You must take your medicine 
everyday. Weigh yourself every morning, call doctor if weight 
goes up more than 3 lbs.  You are deciding to leave against 
medical advice. We believe you are still in heart failure but 
you have decided to leave despite our concern.

You also had signs of withdrawing from alcohol. We had hoped you 
would stay another day to make sure you did not have any issues 
with stopping alcohol, but you wanted to go home. Please talk to 
your doctor about alcohol detoxification programs. 

Please continue to take all of your medications. At the least 
you MUST take your TORSEMIDE, SPIRONOLACTONE, and LISINOPRIL. 
Failure to take these medications will result in worsening of 
your heart failure.

Also, please refrain from alcohol. Heavy alcohol use will also 
worsen your heart failure and can cause liver disease.

It was a pleasure taking care of you,
Sincerely,

- Your ___ Team
